facts.quote: an offsetting charge for service fees charged by LU to the Federated Universities … (calculated as 15% of grant and tuition revenues distributed to the Federated Universities)

facts.text: LU's Board has 21 voting and 9 non-voting members, with FOUR voting positions vacant. The Senate has 77 voting and 6 non-voting members.
facts.quote: The Board is currently comprised of 21 voting members and 9 non-voting members. Four voting member positions are vacant.

facts.text: The Monitor recommends a court-appointed mediator, preferably a sitting or recently retired judge, on an urgent basis; the LU–LUFA relationship is 'currently strained'.
facts.quote: The Proposed Monitor notes the relationship between the Applicant and LUFA is currently strained.

must_not_miss.text: The Monitor's reliability caveat: it quotes Haché's own affidavit saying LU "has experienced a number of challenges with the limited team and resources in the Finance department", and concludes "the Information relied upon for purposes of this Report may be limited by these challenges."
must_not_miss.why: The Monitor is telling the Court, on page 3, that LU's own numbers may not be trustworthy. Buried in boilerplate disclaimer language that extractors are trained to skip.

must_not_miss.text: The Haché affidavit is described as "sworn January 30, 2020" — a year before the report's own date of January 30, 2021 (elsewhere, and in the Pension Order, it is 2021).
must_not_miss.why: A DATE ERROR IN THE SOURCE. Recorded here so scoring can tell the difference between an extractor faithfully reporting the document's stated (wrong) date — which is CORRECT extraction — and one silently "fixing" it to 2021. Both behaviours are interesting; neither should be scored as a miss.

must_not_miss.text: The co-mingling of restricted funds, and the December 2020 creation of three Segregated Accounts.
must_not_miss.why: The core governance failure in the entire Laurentian story — restricted research grants and donations spent on operations. It appears in the middle of a procedural section titled "Cash Management", which reads like plumbing.

must_not_miss.text: LU's proportionate share of SNOLab's assets, liabilities and obligations is 20%.
must_not_miss.why: A quantified off-balance-sheet exposure to a national physics facility, in one clause.

must_not_miss.text: Dr. Haché, LU's President, serves as CHAIR of NOSM's board.
must_not_miss.why: The president of the insolvent university chairs the board of the related party it owes money to and holds $14M of endowments for. Stated once, in passing.

must_not_miss.text: The SuRP is a supplementary retirement plan that is UNFUNDED.
must_not_miss.why: One word — 'unfunded' — inside a list item. It is an entire unsecured liability class.

must_not_miss.text: Stikeman Elliott LLP acts as independent counsel to the Proposed Monitor.
must_not_miss.why: A one-sentence paragraph. The Monitor's own law firm, easy to drop.

must_not_miss.text: Pension membership: 406 collecting, 981 active, ~500 deferred — roughly 1,900 people whose retirement depends on an 85.4%-solvent plan.
must_not_miss.why: The human scale of the pension exposure, given only as three numbers in one paragraph.

must_not_miss.text: The Barrie satellite campus has been closed since 2019; LU is one of twenty public universities in Ontario.
must_not_miss.why: Prior retrenchment, mentioned once in a scene-setting paragraph.

must_not_miss.text: The Federated Funding Formula's 15% service fee, and its 1 May 2019 amendment that decreased funding to the Federated Universities.
must_not_miss.why: LU was already squeezing the federated universities two years before disclaiming them entirely. Requires joining a definition on p. 9 with a cost-cutting list on p. 30.

must_not_miss.text: The Provost's 2020 decision to suspend enrolment in 17 academic programs with "very low enrolment" is the subject of an ongoing unfair labour practice complaint and a judicial review brought by LUFA.
must_not_miss.why: Program suspensions a full year before the CCAA filing — the bridge between the FY2019-20 annual report's "sustainable" narrative (see C1) and the insolvency reality, and already contested in court before the restructuring even began.

must_not_miss.text: MIRARCO "has experienced financial difficulties in the last several years, which has resulted in delays in reimbursements to LU" for the payroll and benefits LU fronts on its behalf.
must_not_miss.why: Explains part of LU's cash erosion: it was carrying the operating costs of its own mining-research affiliate on reimbursements that came back late, buried in a routine description of the payroll arrangement.

X.summary: This is the pre-filing report of Ernst & Young Inc. as Proposed Monitor, prepared in connection with Laurentian University of Sudbury's application for an initial order under the CCAA filed January 30, 2021. The report provides the court with an overview of LU's operations, financial position, cash management practices, and the circumstances driving the filing: five consecutive years of operating deficits, a provincial tuition cut and freeze, declining domestic enrolment, heavy capital-project debt, and COVID-19 pressures that together produced a combined accumulated unrestricted and employee-benefits deficit of approximately $42.6 million and an immediate inability to meet February payroll. LU had total assets of $358.5 million and total recorded liabilities of $321.8 million as at April 30, 2020, but minimal liquid cash; its lines of credit had been cancelled or voluntarily frozen, and without DIP financing from Firm Capital Mortgage Fund Inc. and CCAA protection, operations could not continue beyond February 2021. The report endorses the proposed Initial Order, supports the appointment of a Court-Appointed Mediator (preferably a sitting or recently retired judge), and confirms EY's consent to act as Monitor.

key_facts.fact: Laurentian University of Sudbury filed for CCAA protection on January 30, 2021, seeking a stay of proceedings to allow financial and operational restructuring.
key_facts.quote: LU is insolvent and absent the relief sought in the Initial Order, will not have sufficient funding / liquidity to meet payroll in February.

key_facts.fact: Ernst & Young Inc. was proposed as Monitor for the CCAA proceedings; the firm retained Stikeman Elliott LLP as its independent counsel.
LU was incorporated on March 28, 1960 under An Act to Incorporate Laurentian University of Sudbury, S.O. 1960, c. 151 C. 154.
LU is a non-share capital corporation and a registered charity exempt from income tax under section 149 of the Income Tax Act.
LU had total assets of approximately $358.5 million and total recorded liabilities (including deferred contributions) of approximately $321.8 million as at April 30, 2020.
As at April 30, 2020, LU had minimal liquid assets: approximately $2.6 million in cash and $1.9 million in short-term investments.
LU's investment accounts at SEI Private Trust Company and RBC Dominion Securities Inc. held $54.7 million as at April 30, 2020, with the majority ($52.8 million) designated to support endowments.

LU's capital assets had a net book value of approximately $272.2 million as at April 30, 2020, comprised of buildings ($249.6 million), equipment ($7.3 million), site improvements ($1.9 million), and land ($13.4 million).
LU's net assets declined by $32.9 million over five years, from $69.6 million in fiscal 2014-2015 to $36.7 million in fiscal 2019-2020.
LU's combined accumulated unrestricted fund deficit and employee liabilities deficit had grown to approximately $42.6 million by the time of the CCAA filing.
LU generated deficits in four of the five fiscal years ending April 30, 2016–2020; the only surplus year was 2017-2018 ($2.060 million). The deficit for fiscal 2019-2020 was $3.120 million.

Salaries and benefits were LU's largest expense at approximately 67% of total expenses ($134.6 million) for fiscal year ended April 30, 2020; of this, $16 million related to research, MIRARCO, and SNOLab employees.
The Province of Ontario required all universities to reduce domestic tuition by 10% for 2019-2020 and then imposed a freeze for 2020-2021.

Total fall-semester enrolment (FTE) declined from 7,246 in 2015-2016 to 6,758 in 2018-2019, before recovering slightly to 7,090 in 2020-2021; the 2020-2021 increase of 3.7% was primarily driven by a 36.7% growth in online enrolment, while first-year program enrolment declined 2.3%.

LU previously operated a satellite campus in Barrie, Ontario in partnership with Georgian College; the arrangement expired in 2014, a closure decision was made in 2016, and the campus closed in May 2019.
The Barrie closure created an obligation under the LUFA collective agreement to retain faculty previously associated with that campus.
As at December 30, 2020, LU employed approximately 1,751 people: approximately 758 full-time and 993 fixed-term, part-time, and student employees.
Of LU's approximately 612 LUFA-represented employees, 355 are full-time faculty (many tenured), 252 are sessional faculty or health care professionals, and 5 are full-time counsellors.
The LUFA collective agreement expired on June 30, 2020; bargaining commenced in April 2020, and despite use of a mediator, no material progress had been made on a new agreement as of the filing date.

There were approximately 102 active unresolved LUFA grievances, an ongoing unfair labour practice complaint, and a judicial review of the Provost's 2020 decision to suspend enrolment in 17 low-enrolment academic programs.

LUSU agreed to a renegotiated collective agreement including a 1% salary reduction in Year 1 (previously a 1.5% increase), furlough days generating a one-time $450,000 cash benefit to LU, and 11.5 position redundancies generating approximately $800,000 in annual savings.

LU's DB Pension Plan had a solvency ratio of 85.4% and a going concern deficiency of approximately $4.5 million per the January 1, 2020 actuarial valuation (updated December 2020); annual current service contributions were set at $16,188,000 plus a $505,000 annual special payment to address the deficiency.
LU intended to seek CCAA court relief to stay both pre-filing and post-filing special DB Pension Plan payments to address its liquidity crisis.
The SuRP was unfunded; as at April 30, 2020 the accrued benefit obligation was approximately $3,063,000, with approximately $260,000 forecast to be paid to 32 retirees in July 2021.

The RHBP policy required LU to establish a trust account for contributions, but LU had historically tracked contributions as a liability and co-mingled the funds with operating accounts rather than setting them aside separately.
key_facts.quote: Rather than establishing a separate trust account, LU has historically tracked contributions to the RHBP as a liability in its accounting records and on its balance sheet. However, neither contributions by employees nor LU contributions to the RHBP were set aside in a separate bank account.

key_facts.fact: In December 2020, the Board of Governors directed management to create three new segregated bank accounts (Unspent Research Grant Account, Restricted Funds Account, RHBP Account) to begin separating newly received restricted funds from operating funds, effective December 21, 2020.

Historically, all receipts — including restricted research grants, restricted donations, and RHBP contributions — were deposited into LU's general operating accounts and co-mingled; no separate accounts existed for restricted funds.

As at January 29, 2021, LU had approximately $13.3 million in its operating accounts and approximately $3.3 million in the new Segregated Accounts, but insufficient cash to fund operations beyond February.

The 13-week Cash Flow Forecast (January 30 – April 30, 2021) projects total receipts of approximately $29.5 million and total disbursements of approximately $58.5 million, resulting in a projected net cash outflow of approximately $29.0 million.
LU holds approximately $14 million in endowments designated for NOSM student scholarships; the majority were received before NOSM was incorporated.

Desjardins (Caisse Populaire Voyageurs Inc.) provided LU with an unsecured revolving demand loan of up to $26 million; as at April 30, 2020, $14.4 million was drawn. LU subsequently agreed not to draw further amounts and the facility is currently undrawn.
RBC cancelled its $5 million unsecured revolving line of credit to LU after discussions about LU's financial position.
As at January 29, 2021, the aggregate principal outstanding under the RBC Credit Facilities Agreement was approximately $71.1 million across four non-revolving term facilities.
RBC's credit facilities agreement required LU to covenant not to grant any charge, security interest, or encumbrance on its assets without RBC's written consent.
As at January 29, 2021, the aggregate principal outstanding under the TD Credit Facilities Agreement was approximately $18.5 million across two single-draw reducing term facilities.
Approximately $1.3 million was outstanding under the BMO Credit Facility as of the report date; BMO agreed to defer principal payments in June 2020 due to COVID-19.
LU guaranteed the SGA's $8.5 million debt to TD pursuant to a guarantee dated June 27, 2018, arising from a letter agreement between SGA and TD dated April 10, 2018 for a new student centre.
Interest rate swaps with LU's lenders resulted in a net cash outflow of approximately $340,000 monthly to LU.
LU's monthly aggregate payroll is approximately $11 million, monthly DB Pension Plan contributions are approximately $1.2 million, and monthly vacation pay accrual is approximately $800,000.

LU executed a DIP term sheet with Firm Capital Corporation, which subsequently assigned its interest to Firm Capital Mortgage Fund Inc. as DIP Lender; the DIP Agreement was to be finalized before the comeback hearing.
The Proposed Initial Order provides for a first-ranking Administration Charge of up to $400,000 and a second-ranking Directors' Charge of up to $2 million, both on LU's assets.

The SGA was proposed as a Non-Applicant Stay Party, with the stay limited to preventing proceedings against it and contract terminations arising from LU's insolvency; SGA has approximately $8.5 million in long-term debt.

The Proposed Monitor recommended the Court appoint a Court-Appointed Mediator — preferably a sitting or recently retired judge with experience in both insolvency and labour negotiations — to oversee restructuring negotiations with LUFA and other parties.
The Cash Flow Forecast projects two DIP financing draws totalling $25 million: $9.5 million in week 2 and $15 million in week 7, resulting in a $25 million DIP balance outstanding at April 30, 2021.
MIRARCO has experienced financial difficulties in recent years, resulting in delays in reimbursements to LU for payroll, benefits, and pension plan contributions funded by LU on MIRARCO's behalf.
The Federated Funding Formula was amended and restated on May 1, 2019, reducing the amount of funding distributed by LU to the Federated Universities.

Of LU's 132 undergraduate programs, 25% of students are in the top 5 programs and 83% are in the top 50; only 5% of students are enrolled in the bottom 50 programs, indicating severe concentration and a large number of financially unsustainable programs.

Dr. Robert Haché's affidavit, sworn January 30, 2021 (noted in the report as January 30, 2020 — a likely typographic error), acknowledged that LU's Finance department faced significant resource challenges that may have limited the accuracy of the financial information.
key_facts.quote: LU has experienced a number of challenges with the limited team and resources in the Finance department, and such difficulties are made even more pronounced with the additional demands placed on their time in connection with the preparation for this CCAA proceeding.

key_facts.fact: Sharon S. Hamilton, CPA, CA, CIRP, LIT, Senior Vice President of Ernst & Young Inc., signed the report.

Y.summary: This is the pre-filing report of Ernst & Young Inc. as Proposed Monitor, submitted to the Ontario Superior Court of Justice (Commercial List) on January 30, 2021, in connection with Laurentian University of Sudbury's application for protection under the Companies' Creditors Arrangement Act. The report establishes that LU is insolvent and will be unable to meet its February payroll without CCAA protection and DIP financing; it describes EY's qualifications, LU's governance and operations, the financial position as at April 30, 2020 (total assets $358.5 million, total liabilities including deferred contributions $321.8 million, accumulated unrestricted and employee-liabilities deficit of approximately $42.6 million), the circumstances driving the insolvency (recurring deficits, 10% tuition cut mandated by Ontario in 2019, declining domestic enrolment, heavy capital borrowing, COVID-19 impacts, and stalled LUFA bargaining), and the proposed DIP facility with Firm Capital Mortgage Fund Inc. The report also addresses the proposed super-priority charges (Administration Charge up to $400,000 and Directors' Charge up to $2 million), the stay of proceedings for the SGA as a Non-Applicant Stay Party, and the Monitor's recommendation for the Court to appoint an independent mediator, preferably a sitting or recently retired judge, to oversee restructuring negotiations.

key_facts.fact: Laurentian University of Sudbury filed for CCAA protection on January 30, 2021, citing insolvency and an inability to meet its February payroll without court protection and DIP financing.
key_facts.quote: LU is insolvent and absent the relief sought in the Initial Order, will not have sufficient funding / liquidity to meet payroll in February.

key_facts.fact: Ernst & Young Inc. was proposed as Monitor for the CCAA proceedings, with Stikeman Elliott LLP retained as EY's independent counsel.

LU was incorporated on March 28, 1960 under An Act to Incorporate Laurentian University of Sudbury, S.O. 1960, c. 151 C. 154, and is a non-share capital corporation and registered charity exempt from income tax under section 149 of the Income Tax Act.
key_facts.quote: On March 28, 1960, LU was incorporated under An Act to Incorporate Laurentian University of Sudbury, S.O. 1960, c. 151 C. 154

key_facts.fact: LU is a publicly funded, bilingual and tricultural post-secondary institution located in the City of Greater Sudbury, Ontario, and has consistently been one of the largest employers in Sudbury.
The Board of Governors has 21 voting members and 9 non-voting members; four voting member positions are vacant. The Senate has 77 voting members and 6 non-voting members.

As of the 2020-2021 fall semester, LU had approximately 8,200 domestic and international undergraduate students (approximately 6,250 full-time equivalents) and approximately 1,100 graduate students (approximately 830 full-time equivalents).
LU holds approximately $14 million in endowments designated to fund future NOSM student scholarships; the majority of these funds were received prior to NOSM's incorporation.

LU and Lakehead University are the two members of the Northern Ontario School of Medicine (NOSM), a not-for-profit corporation that serves as the faculty of medicine for both universities; NOSM opened in 2005.
key_facts.quote: Through an agreement between LU and Lakehead, located in Thunder Bay, Ontario, NOSM opened in 2005.

key_facts.fact: LU owns the two buildings that NOSM occupies on the Sudbury campus and leases them to NOSM.
NOSM student registration fees for certain students are deposited into LU's general operating accounts and remitted to NOSM net of service fees charged by LU.

The Federated Universities (University of Sudbury, Huntington University, and Thorneloe University) each own buildings on land owned by LU and leased to them; they do not receive provincial operating grants directly and rely on LU's Federated Funding Formula for revenue.
Employees of the Federated Universities are members of LU's pension plan and each Federated University contributes directly to the DB Pension Plan monthly.
LU charges the Federated Universities a service fee equal to 15% of grant and tuition revenues distributed to them under the Federated Funding Formula.

SNOLab is an underground research laboratory located in Vale's Creighton mine near Sudbury, operated under a trust agreement among five institutions: LU, Carleton University, Queen's University, University of Alberta, and Université de Montréal. LU's proportionate share of SNOLab assets, liabilities, and obligations is 20%.
As of December 2020, LU processed payroll for approximately 128 SNOLab employees and provided their benefit programs; SNOLab reimburses LU in full.

MIRARCO is a not-for-profit mining research arm of LU headquartered in Sudbury; LU is its sole member and MIRARCO is consolidated in LU's financial statements. MIRARCO has experienced financial difficulties in recent years, causing delays in reimbursements to LU.
LU processed payroll for MIRARCO's 19 employees and for CEMI's 5 employees, funding their payroll and benefits and invoicing for reimbursement.
As at December 30, 2020, LU employed approximately 1,751 people: roughly 758 full-time and 993 fixed-term, part-time, and student employees.
key_facts.quote: As at December 30, 2020, LU employed approximately 1,751 people.

key_facts.fact: Of LU's approximately 612 LUFA employees, 355 are full-time faculty (many tenured), 252 are sessional faculty or health care professionals, and 5 are full-time counsellors.

LUFA provided LU with a notice to bargain in February 2020; the LUFA collective agreement (expiring June 30, 2020) has been auto-continuing during negotiations. Despite bargaining with mediator assistance, no material progress has been made on a new collective agreement.

There are approximately 102 active unresolved LUFA grievances, plus an ongoing unfair labour practice complaint and a judicial review of the Provost's 2020 decision to suspend enrolment in 17 low-enrolment academic programs.

LUSU and LU entered into a collective agreement on July 1, 2018, set to expire June 30, 2021. LUSU subsequently agreed to open it early; the amended agreement included a 1.0% salary reduction in Year 1 and six unpaid furlough days in 2020.
key_facts.quote: Year 1: a 1.0% salary reduction, which previously was a 1.5% salary increase under the LUSU CA

key_facts.fact: The LUSU furlough days provided LU a one-time cash benefit of $450,000 paid directly by LUSU; the reassignment, transfer, and retirement provisions generated 11.5 position redundancies and approximately $800,000 in annual savings.

CUPE and LU entered into a collective agreement on September 1, 2019 (expiring August 31, 2021); CUPE agreed to a 1% total compensation increase allocated entirely to scholarships, with 0% salary increase over the two-year term.

LU administers three employee benefit plans: a registered defined benefit pension plan (DB Pension Plan), a supplementary unfunded retirement plan (SuRP, implemented July 1, 2002), and a retirement health benefits plan (RHBP).

As at January 1, 2020, the DB Pension Plan had a solvency ratio of 85.4% and a going concern deficiency of approximately $4.5 million, requiring a special annual payment contribution of $505,000 (approximately $42,083/month) in addition to current service contributions of $16,188,000 annually ($1,349,000/month).
LU sought relief in the CCAA proceedings to stay both pre-filing and post-filing special payments to the DB Pension Plan.

The SuRP is unfunded; 32 retired employees are eligible for payments. The forecast SuRP payment due in July 2021 is approximately $260,000. As at April 30, 2020, the accrued SuRP benefit obligation was approximately $3,063,000. SuRP payments are stayed under the proposed CCAA order.
LU has contractual agreements to provide supplemental retirement benefits to two individuals in former or current leadership roles; these obligations are unfunded and are proposed to be stayed.

The RHBP policy required LU to establish a trust account funded by employee premiums, an annual $25,000 LU contribution, and proportionate Federated University contributions. Instead, LU tracked these as a balance-sheet liability and did not segregate the funds in a separate bank account until directed by the Board in December 2020.
LU does not prepare interim monthly or quarterly financial statements; the most recent available financial statements are the audited annual statements for the year ended April 30, 2020.

LU generated a deficiency of revenues over expenses of $3,120,000 in fiscal 2019-2020 (year ended April 30, 2020), continuing a pattern of recurring losses: deficits of $1,986,000 (2015-16), $1,822,000 (2016-17), and $4,100,000 (2018-19), with a single surplus of $2,060,000 in 2017-18.

Salaries and benefits represented approximately 67% of total expenses for fiscal year ended April 30, 2020, totalling $134,552,000 including $16 million attributable to research, MIRARCO, and SNOLab employees; the remaining $119 million relates to academic teaching and ancillary services.

As at April 30, 2020, LU had total assets of $358,520,000, total current assets of $33,239,000 (including $4,544,000 in cash and short-term investments and $27,045,000 in accounts receivable), and capital assets with a net book value of $272,267,000.

As at April 30, 2020, LU had approximately $2.6 million in cash and $1.9 million in short-term investments; total recorded liabilities (including deferred contributions of $168,398,000) were approximately $321.8 million. Net assets were $36,682,000.

LU's capital assets as at April 30, 2020 had a net book value of $272.2 million, comprised of buildings ($249.6 million), equipment ($7.3 million), site improvements ($1.9 million), and land ($13.4 million). Properties include the main campus, the Art Centre at 251 John Street, the President's House, and the McEwen School of Architecture at 85 Elm Street in downtown Sudbury.

LU's net assets declined by $32.9 million, from $69.6 million in fiscal year 2014-2015 to $36.7 million in fiscal year 2019-2020. The unrestricted fund deficit was $20.0 million and the vacation/employee future benefits fund deficit was $22.6 million as at April 30, 2020.
LU's combined accumulated unrestricted fund deficit and employee liabilities deficit had grown to approximately $42.6 million at the time of the CCAA filing.

LU historically maintained investment accounts at SEI Private Trust Company and RBC Dominion Securities Inc.; the balance was $54.7 million as at April 30, 2020, of which approximately $52.8 million supported endowments (including $14.0 million for NOSM student scholarships).

LU had two unsecured revolving lines of credit: a Desjardins (Caisse Populaire Voyageurs Inc.) line of up to $26 million and an RBC line of up to $5 million. As at April 30, 2020, $14.4 million was drawn on the Desjardins line; the RBC line was undrawn. Both facilities are now unavailable: RBC cancelled its line and LU agreed not to draw on the Desjardins line.

LU has a TD credit facility (TD Credit Facility Agreement dated October 3, 2005, as amended May 30, 2008, June 1, 2009, and July 27, 2016) providing a $2.0 million reducing term facility (maturity April 3, 2021) with $1,323,626 outstanding as of January 29, 2021, and two additional term facilities with $10,575,875 and $6,570,917 outstanding as of January 29, 2021, for aggregate TD principal outstanding of approximately $18.5 million.

LU has unsecured long-term debt with BMO, RBC, and TD totalling approximately $91.7 million as at April 30, 2020, with maturities ranging from 2023 to 2043. RBC facilities alone total approximately $71.1 million (four non-revolving term facilities originally totalling $75.4 million).
Pursuant to the RBC Credit Facilities Agreement, LU covenanted not to grant any security interest on its assets without RBC's written consent.
LU guaranteed the SGA's $8,500,000 obligation to TD under a guarantee dated June 27, 2018, in connection with a Letter Agreement between SGA and TD dated April 10, 2018 for a new student centre.
LU's interest rate swaps resulted in a net cash outflow of approximately $340,000 per month.

Deferred contributions as at April 30, 2020 totalled $38.5 million (estimated to be $36.5 million as of December 31, 2020); no funds were set aside to satisfy these obligations. Deferred capital contributions were $129.9 million ($0.6 million unspent, $129.3 million unamortized), also without funds set aside.

In December 2020, the Board directed management to create three new segregated bank accounts (Unspent Research Grant Account, Restricted Funds Account, RHBP Account) to begin segregating newly received restricted funds and RHBP contributions, effective December 21, 2020. Prior to this, all receipts including restricted funds were co-mingled in operating accounts.

Z.summary:
This 47-page proposed monitor report supports Laurentian University of Sudbury’s January 30, 2021 CCAA application and the appointment of Ernst & Young Inc. as monitor so the court can grant a stay of proceedings and give the university breathing room to restructure. The report says Laurentian, a publicly funded Ontario university incorporated in 1960, was insolvent, faced an immediate liquidity crisis, and without CCAA relief and DIP funding would be unable to meet February payroll or continue through the academic term.

The monitor describes a university with about $358.5 million in assets and the same amount in liabilities, deferred contributions and net assets as of April 30, 2020, but with mounting operating strain, including a $3.1 million annual deficit, a $42.6 million combined unrestricted-fund and employee-liability deficit, and long-term debt of about $91.7 million. Key pressures included a 2020 Ontario tuition reduction and freeze, COVID-related enrollment and staffing disruptions, deferred payments on major credit facilities, a $4.5 million going-concern pension deficiency, and unfunded or underfunded benefit obligations; the report also notes that the university had not set aside funds for deferred contributions and had only recently begun segregating restricted money such as RHBP contributions.

The proposed restructuring would allow Laurentian to keep paying ordinary-course wages, benefits, student refunds, and certain student-association amounts while obtaining a DIP facility from Firm Capital and court charges securing professional fees and directors’ indemnities. The report also asks for a limited stay for the Student General Association because Laurentian guaranteed about $8.5 million of its debt, and says the restructuring must address the federated universities model, academic programs, and employee headcount reductions to reach a sustainable cost structure.

key_facts.fact: In December 2020, Laurentian University of Sudbury's board directed management to create three segregated bank accounts for unspent research grants, restricted funds, and RHBP contributions.
key_facts.quote: The Board instructed management to amend its practice and immediately create three new bank accounts

key_facts.fact: As of January 29, 2021, Laurentian University of Sudbury estimated cash of $13.3 million in operating accounts and $3.3 million in segregated accounts.
key_facts.quote: approximately $13.3 million

key_facts.fact: The report says Laurentian University of Sudbury expected to need significant cash outflow and lacked sufficient cash to fund operations through February or beyond.
key_facts.quote: the Applicant currently has insufficient cash to fund operations through the month of February or beyond.

key_facts.fact: Laurentian University of Sudbury prepared a 13-week cash flow forecast for January 30, 2021 through the week ending April 30, 2021, and the Proposed Monitor reviewed it under the CCAA reasonableness standard.
key_facts.quote: The Applicant, with the assistance of the Proposed Monitor, has prepared a Cash Flow Forecast for the 13 week period from January 30, 2021 to the week ending April 30, 2021.

key_facts.fact: The Proposed Monitor said its review of the cash flow forecast relied on management-supplied information and assumptions and found nothing causing it to believe the forecast was unreasonable in material respects.
key_facts.quote: nothing has come to its attention that causes it to believe, in all material respects, that...

key_facts.fact: The cash flow forecast projected approximately $29.5 million of receipts, $58.5 million of disbursements, and $29.0 million of net cash outflow over the 13-week period, assuming court approval of DIP financing.
key_facts.quote: This results in projected net cash outflow ... of approximately $29.0 million.

key_facts.fact: Laurentian University of Sudbury executed a DIP term sheet with Firm Capital Corporation, which later assigned its interest to Firm Capital Mortgage Fund Inc.
key_facts.quote: Firm Capital Corporation assigned its interest to Firm Capital Mortgage Fund Inc. (the 'DIP Lender').

key_facts.fact: The report says the SGA should receive a limited stay of proceedings because Laurentian University of Sudbury guaranteed about $8.5 million of the SGA's debt and the SGA depends on Laurentian's continued operations and fee collection.
key_facts.quote: The insolvency of LU puts the SGA in a highly vulnerable position.

key_facts.fact: The proposed initial order would let Laurentian University of Sudbury pay ordinary-course student amounts and remit students' association fees, with about $1.6 million forecast to be remitted during the cash flow period.
key_facts.quote: The amount forecast to be remitted during the Cash Flow Period is approximately $1.6 million

key_facts.fact: The proposed initial order would create an Administration Charge up to $400,000 and a Directors' Charge up to $2 million on Laurentian University of Sudbury's assets.
key_facts.quote: first, the Administration Charge (up to a maximum amount of $400,000); and second, the Directors' Charge (up to a maximum amount of $2 million).

key_facts.fact: The report says Laurentian University of Sudbury's secured creditors are mainly subcontractors with construction liens and limited equipment lessors.
key_facts.quote: The Applicant's secured creditors are primarily comprised of subcontractors who have registered construction liens... and limited equipment lessors.

key_facts.fact: LU forecast remitting approximately $1.6 million in student-association fees during the cash-flow period, much of it already collected before the proposed CCAA commencement date, and treats those funds as belonging to the Students' Associations rather than to LU.

The Proposed Monitor supports limited stay-of-proceedings exceptions for remittance of those student-association amounts, saying the prejudice to stakeholders is outweighed by the benefit of protecting students and vulnerable parties.

The Proposed Initial Order would create an Administration Charge of up to $400,000 and a Directors' Charge of up to $2 million, both secured on all of LU's current and future assets, undertakings and property wherever located and ranking in that order.

The Administration Charge is intended to secure professional fees and disbursements for counsel and advisors to LU, the Proposed Monitor, the Proposed Monitor's independent counsel, and independent counsel to the Board.

The Directors' Charge is intended to secure an indemnity for current and future directors and officers of LU for post-commencement actions, except where liability arises from gross negligence or willful misconduct.

The Proposed Monitor says LU's monthly payroll is approximately $11 million, monthly DB Pension Plan contributions are approximately $1.2 million, and monthly vacation pay accrual is approximately $800,000, and that the proposed $2 million Directors' Charge is less than the amount of those liabilities that will accrue in the first 10 days.
LU plans to seek a DIP Lender's Charge to match the maximum allowable borrowing amount under the proposed DIP Term Sheet, which is a condition of the financing.
The proposed court-appointed mediator is meant to oversee restructuring negotiations covering LU's Federated Universities model, academic programs, and employee headcount reductions.

The Proposed Monitor says LU is facing an immediate liquidity crisis, and without CCAA protection and DIP funding it would be unable to meet February payroll, continue through the academic term, or avoid an immediate shutdown.

The Proposed Monitor says the DIP Term Sheet should carry LU through the end of the current academic term, but LU still must complete a comprehensive financial and operational restructuring within that period to reach a sustainable cost structure.
The Proposed Monitor recommends that the court appoint an independent, objective mediator with insolvency and labour-negotiation experience, preferably a sitting or recently retired judge.
Ernst & Young Inc., acting as Proposed Monitor, consents to serve as monitor of LU if the court grants the requested relief.

The monitor's cash-flow forecast assumes an exchange rate of CDN$1.30 = US$1.00, assumes financing under the DIP Term Sheet, and assumes that pre-filing amounts owed to third-party suppliers and service providers are stayed while post-filing goods and services are paid in the ordinary course.

The forecast assumes operating grants will continue from the Province of Ontario on a semi-monthly basis, research grants will follow the Applicant's research-group forecast and past funding experience, and student fees will be collected seasonally after registration.
The forecast assumes payroll and ordinary-course benefits, pension contributions, and vacation pay will be paid, while statutory deductions such as CPP, QPP, and income tax will be remitted.
The forecast says student refunds and student scholarship, bursary, or grant amounts for the 2020-21 academic year and future periods will be paid in the ordinary course.

The forecast assumes transfers of research grants to other researchers or research partners, transfers to Federated Universities under LU's post-filing funding formula obligations, and transfers to NOSM and Students' Associations based on post-filing billing and collection of the relevant student fees.

The forecast assumes capital-project disbursements have been reduced because certain projects were deferred, debt service is stayed as of the CCAA filing date, endowment funds include LU and NOSM scholarship funds, and restricted receipts are held in segregated accounts for restricted use.
The forecast assumes restructuring costs will be paid on anticipated run rates and that assistants retained or employed by LU will be paid.
The forecast assumes the proposed DIP facility will be advanced in two tranches under the DIP Term Sheet.
